Commerce_buy.definition:
<def-root>These are words describing a basic commercial transaction involving a <fen>Buyer</fen> and a <fen>Seller</fen> exchanging <fen>Money</fen> and <fen>Goods</fen>, taking the perspective of the <fen>Buyer</fen>.  The words vary individually in the patterns of frame element realization they allow.  For example, the typical pattern for the verb BUY:
<fen>Buyer</fen> buys <fen>Goods</fen> from <fen>Seller</fen> for <fen>Money</fen>.
<ex></ex>
<ex><fex name="Buyer">Abby</fex> bought <fex name="Goods">a car</fex> <fex name="Seller">from Robin</fex> <fex name="Money">for $5,000</fex>.</ex></def-root>

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Buyer</fen> wants the <fen>Goods</fen> and offers <fen>Money</fen> to a <fen>Seller</fen> in exchange for them.
<ex><fex name="Buyer">Jess</fex> <t>bought</t> a coat.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Buyer">Lee</fex> <t>bought</t> a textbook from Abby.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Buyer

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The FE <fen>Goods</fen> is anything (including labor or time, for example) which is exchanged for <fen>Money</fen> in a transaction. 
<ex> Only one winner <t>purchased</t> <fex name="Gds">the paintings</fex></ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Goods

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Means</fen> by which a commercial transaction occurs.
<ex> Will they allow you to <t>purchase</t> <fex name="Mns">by check</fex>? </ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Means

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root><fen>Money</fen> is the thing given in exchange for <fen>Goods</fen> in a transaction.
<ex>Sam <t>bought</t> the car <fex name="Money">for $12,000</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Money

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>In some cases, price or payment is described per unit of <fen>Goods</fen>.
<ex> Jon <t>bought</t> some expensive apples <fex name="Rate">at five dollars a pound</fex>! </ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Rate

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Seller</fen> has possession of the <fen>Goods</fen> and exchanges them for <fen>Money</fen> from a <fen>Buyer</fen>.
<ex>Most of my audio equipment, I <t>purchased</t> <fex name="Seller">from a department store near my apartment</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Seller

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE is any unit in which goods or services can be measured.
Generally, it occurs in a <ment>by</ment>-PP. 
<ex>Lee <t>buys</t> potatoes <fex name="Unit">by the pound</fex>. </ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Unit

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>Where the event takes place.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Place

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Purpose</fen> for which an intentional act is performed.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Purpose

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fex name="Explanation">Explanation</fex> for which an event occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Explanation

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>When the event occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Time

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>Any description of the purchasing event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including secondary effects (<ment>quietly, loudly</ment>), and general descriptions comparing events (<ment>the same way</ment>). It may also indicate salient characteristics of the <fen>Buyer</fen> that affect the action (<ment>presumptuously, coldly, deliberately, eagerly, carefully</ment>).
<ex>She <fex name="Manner">gleefully</fex> <t>bought</t> the rock.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Manner

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The individual intended by the <fen>Buyer</fen> to receive the <fen>Goods</fen>.
<ex>You <t>bought</t> <fex name="Recipient">me</fex> three pairs already!</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Recipient

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The length of time from when the commerce event began to be repeated to when it stopped.
<ex>I have been <t>buying</t> from him <fex name="iter">for over 10 years</fex>.</ex>
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Period_of_iterations

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Buyer</fen>'s intended purpose for the <fen>Goods</fen>.
<ex>I <t>purchased</t> the calculator<fex name="Imposed_purpose">for easier calculation of my debts</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Imposed_purpose

Desiring.definition:
<def-root>An <fen>Experiencer</fen> desires that an <fen>Event</fen> occur.  (Note that commonly a resultant state of the <fen>Event</fen> will stand in for the <fen>Event</fen>.)  In some cases, the <fen>Experiencer</fen> is an active participant in the <fen>Event</fen>, and in such cases the <fen>Event</fen> itself is often not mentioned, but rather some <fen>Focal_participant</fen> which is subordinately involved in the <fen>Event</fen>. <ex></ex>Generally, the use of a word in this frame implies that the specific <fen>Event</fen> has not yet happened, but that the <fen>Experiencer</fen> believes that they would be happier if it did.  Sometimes the <fen>Time_of_event</fen>, <fen>Purpose_of_event</fen>, or the <fen>Location_of_event</fen> are mentioned without the explicit mention of the <fen>Event</fen>.
<ex><fex name="Experiencer">I</fex> only <t>wanted</t> <fex name="Foc">one piece of candy</fex>.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Exp">The company</fex> <m>was</m> <t>eager</t> <fex name="Foc">for him</fex> <fex name="Event">to leave as soon as possible</fex>.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Exp">Susan</fex> <fex name="Degr">really</fex> <t>wishes</t> <fex name="Event">that you 'd listen to her</fex>.</ex></def-root>

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Experiencer</fen> is the person (or sentient being) who wishes for the <fen>Event</fen> to occur.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Experiencer

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The change that the <fen>Experiencer</fen> would like to see.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Event

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>This is the entity that the <fen>Experiencer</fen> wishes to be affected by some <fen>Event</fen>.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Focal_participant

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Degree</fen> is a the extent of the <fen>Experiencer</fen>'s Desiring.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Degree

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The way in which the <fen>Experiencer</fen> desires something.

<ex>I <t>wanted</t> more of her <fex name="Manner">like a junkie wants his next fix</fex>.</ex>

</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Manner

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>An aspect of the <fen>Experiencer</fen> that causes a desire.
<ex>Do Italians have a <fex name="Explanation">genetic</fex> <t>yearning</t> for pizza?</ex>
<ex><fex name="Explanation">Intellectually</fex> he <t>longed</t> for success, but really he just wanted love.</ex>
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Explanation

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Purpose_of_event</fen> is the purpose pertaining to the desired <fen>Event</fen>.

<ex>I <t>want</t> that book <fex name="Purp">for my test tomorrow</fex>.</ex>
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Purpose_of_event

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The time that the <fen>Event</fen> would ideally occur.
<ex>I <t>want</t> porridge <fex name="EvT">tomorrow</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Time_of_event

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Location_of_event</fen> is the place involved in the desired <fen>Event</fen>.

<ex>I <t>want</t> that box <fex name="PEv">on top of the other one</fex>.</ex>
<ex>The prince <t>wishes</t> you <fex name="PEv">here</fex> before matins.</ex>
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Location_of_event

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Time</fen> is when the <fen>Experiencer</fen> desires something.
<ex>Oh, so <fex name="Time">now</fex> you <t>want</t> to go to the zoo!</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Time

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>Where the event takes place.  Note that this FE is of extremely rare occurrence in this frame.
<ex><fex name="Place">In the car</fex> I had <t>desired</t> nothing more than to get here, but now that I'm here...</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Place

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The amount of time for which the <fen>Experiencer</fen> has desired something.
<ex>His <fex name="Dur">lifelong</fex> <t>yearning</t> for success had finally been fulfilled.</ex>
<ex>I've <t>wanted</t> them to fix the sidewalk <fex name="Dur">for years</fex>!</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Duration

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The Role is a role filled by a Focal_participant in the Event that the Experiencer desires.

<ex>Michaels originally <t>wanted</t> Smith <fex name="rol">as the new Late Night producer</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Role_of_focal_participant

Event.definition:
<def-root>An <fen>Event</fen> takes place at a <fen>Place</fen> and <fen>Time</fen>.

<ex><fex name="Event">Big earthquakes</fex> only <t>happen</t> <fex name="Place">along plate boundaries</fex>. <fex name="Time">INI</fex> </ex>

<ex><fex name="Event">The party</fex> will <t>take place</t> <fex name="Time">on Sunday</fex> <fex name="Place">in the all-you-can-eat buffet</fex>.</ex></def-root>

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>Name of the event which occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Event

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>Where the event takes place.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Place

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fex name="Explanation">Explanation</fex> for which an event occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Explanation

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>When the event occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Time

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>How long the <fen>Event</fen> takes place.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Duration

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>Any description of the event which is not covered by more specific FEs, including epistemic modification (<ment>probably, presumably, mysteriously</ment>), force (<ment>hard, softly</ment>), secondary effects (<ment>quietly, loudly</ment>), and general descriptions comparing events (<ment>the same way</ment>).

</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Manner

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>How often the <fen>Event</fen> occurs.
<ex>Stuff like this <t>happens</t> <fex name="Freq">every day</fex> at 3:00pm.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Frequency

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The period within which an <fen>Event</fen> has occurred.

<ex>It was <fex name="Event">the largest food fight</fex> to <t>occur</t> <fex name="Timespan">since the time Jimmy's mom packed him extra Sloppy Joes.</fex></ex>

<ex><fex name="Timespan">From 1992 to 2014</fex>, <fex name="Event">my amazing birthday celebration</fex> has <t>happened</t> <fex name="Frequency">22 times</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Timespan

Motion.definition:
<def-root>Some entity (<fen>Theme</fen>) starts out in one place (<fen>Source</fen>) and ends up in some other place (<fen>Goal</fen>), having covered some space between the two (<fen>Path</fen>). Alternatively, the <fen>Area</fen> or <fen>Direction</fen>in which the <fen>Theme</fen> moves or the <fen>Distance</fen> of the movement may be mentioned.

<ex><fex name="Theme">That kite you see just to the right of his head</fex> was <t>moving</t> <fex name="Area">around</fex> <fex name="Speed">pretty fast</fex> but the camera seemed to catch it ok.</ex>

<ex>There are several accounts of <fex name="Theme">the stench</fex> <t>drifting</t> <fex name="Goal">to shore</fex> <fex name="Source">from the ships in the middle of the river</fex></ex>

<ex><fex name="Theme">Dust particles</fex> <t>floating</t> <fex name="Area">about</fex> made him sneeze uncontrollably.</ex>

<ex><fex name="Theme">The grill</fex>, unsecured, <t>rolled</t> <fex name="Distance">a few feet</fex> <fex name="Path">across the yard</fex>.</ex>

<ex><fex name="Theme">The swarm</fex> <t>went</t> <fex name="Direction">away</fex> <fex name="Goal">to the end of the hall</fex>.</ex>

The frames that inherit the general Motion frame add some elaboration to this simple idea.  Inheriting frames can add Goal-profiling (<ment>arrive, reach</ment>), Source-profiling (<ment>leave, depart</ment>), or Path-profiling (<ment>traverse, cross</ment>), or aspects of the manner of motion (<ment>run, jog</ment>) or assumptions about the shape-properties, etc., of any of the places involved (<ment>insert, extract</ment>).
A particularly complex area in the vocabulary of Motion is the depiction of the relation of Vehicles to the Theme.  In some cases, no separate Theme is expressed:

<ex>The plane <t>flew</t> over the city.</ex> 

In this case, the sentence is annotated in Self_motion.  When the Vehicle is profiled as being operated by a Driver, the sentence is annotated in the Operate_vehicles frame:

<ex>Don't try to <t>fly</t> an F-16 without training!</ex>

This is very similar to the Bringing frame which covers cases where the Vehicle is necessarily involved, but the movement of the <fen>Theme</fen> (something carried by the Vehicle) is profiled:

<ex>It's scary <t>flying</t> hundreds of people over thousands of miles of ocean every day.</ex>

Some of the same vocabulary is also used to describe the situation where Passengers Ride_vehicle or Operate_vehicle (each of these a perspective on Use_vehicles):

<ex>I <t>flew</t> to Chicago on the red-eye.</ex>
<ex>I <t>flew</t> my plane across the Canadian border</ex> 

Finally, there are cases where, despite the use of similar vocabulary, there is no self-propelled Vehicle involved at all:

<ex>The ball <t>flew</t> over the fence.</ex>

This last type is annotated in the simple Motion frame.</def-root>

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Theme</fen> is the entity that changes location. Note that it is not necessarily a self-mover.
<ex>The explosion made <fex name="Thm">me</fex> <t>move</t> in a hurry.</ex> </def-root>
frame_elements.name: Theme

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Source</fen> is the location the <fen>Theme</fen> occupies initially before its change of location.

<ex>The policeman <t>moved</t> <fex name="Src">away from the door</fex>.</ex> </def-root>
frame_elements.name: Source

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Path</fen> refers to (a part of) the ground over which the <fen>Theme</fen> travels  or to a landmark by which the <fen>Theme</fen> travels.

<ex>Jo <t>moved</t> <fex name="Path">past Dad</fex> into the hall.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Path

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Goal</fen> is the location the <fen>Theme</fen> ends up in.

<ex>The car <t>moved</t> <fex name="Goal">into the slow lane</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Goal

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root><fen>Area</fen> identifies the setting in which the <fen>Theme</fen>'s movement takes place without a specified <fen>Path</fen>.

<ex>Emily <t>moved</t> restlessly <fex name="Area">around the room</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Area

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root><fen>Distance</fen> is any expression which characterizes the extent of the Motion. 
<ex>The twig <t>floated</t> atop the water <fex name="Dist">for about 100 yards</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Distance

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE is used for the <fen>Speed</fen> at which the <fen>Theme</fen> moves.

<ex>The ash cloud <t>drifted</t> <fex name="Spd">at twenty-five kilometres per hour</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Speed

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Carrier</fen> is the means of conveyance of the <fen>Theme</fen>.

<ex>The nest <t>blew</t> from its tree <fex name="Car">in a gale</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Carrier

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the <fen>Duration</fen> of  time for which the Motion takes place.

<ex>The balloon <t>floated</t> <fex name="Dur">for  hours</fex>.</ex>
 
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Duration

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the <fen>Time</fen> when the Motion occurs.

<ex>A radioactive cloud <t>drifted</t> across Britain <fex name="Time">after the fire at the Windscale nuclear factory</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Time

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the <fen>Manner</fen> in which the Motion takes place.
<ex>A naval airship <t>drifted</t> <fex name="Manr">wildy</fex> in the stormy sea.</ex>

</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Manner

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root><fen>Result</fen> identifies the ultimate effect of the Motion.
<ex>The feathers <t>floated</t> <fex name="Result">together</fex> on the water's surface.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Result

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>This FE is used for any <fen>Depictive</fen> phrase describing the state of the <fen>Theme</fen> while the motion is occuring.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Depictive

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Place</fen> is the general area in which a specific motion (with <fen>Source</fen>, <fen>Path</fen>, or <fen>Goal</fen>) occurs.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Place

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The extent to which the <fen>Theme</fen> cross a boundary as it moves away from a <fen>Source</fen> region or into a <fen>Goal</fen> region.

<ex>Pluto has <t>moved</t> <fex name="Degree">fully</fex>into Sagittarius</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Degree

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>This FE is used for expressions that indicate motion along a line from the deitic center towards a reference point (which may be implicit) that is neither the <fen>Goal</fen> of the posture change nor a landmark along the way of the moving part of the body.  Often <fen>Direction</fen> is defined with reference to the canonical orientation of the Protagonist, or the orientation imposed by an implicit observer.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Direction

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>In cases wherein the <fen>Theme</fen> is construed as a sentient entity, this FE denotes the state of affairs that the entity wishes to bring about by moving.

<ex>Johnny <t>went</t> to Langley  <fex name="pur">to turn himself in</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Purpose

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The shape of the overall <fen>Path</fen> travelled by the <fen>Theme</fen>.

<ex>They <t>drifted</t> <fex name="sha">in circles</fex> for weeks before rescue .</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Path_shape

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>An event that the described motion forms an integral part of.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Containing_event

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>This frame element is defined as the number of times an event occurs per some unit of time. A Frequency expression answers the question how often. </def-root>
frame_elements.name: Frequency

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The frame element <fex name="Iterations">Iterations</fex> is used for expressions that indicate the number of times an event or state (of the kind denoted by the target in its clause) has taken place or held.</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Iterations

Motion_noise.definition:
<def-root>This frame pertains to noise verbs used to characterize motion.  Motion_noise verbs take largely the same <fen>Source</fen>, <fen>Path</fen> and <fen>Goal</fen> expressions as other types of Motion verbs.

<ex><fex name="Thm">The reception doors</fex> <t>banged</t> <fex name="Result">open</fex>.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Thm">Guillemots and razor bills</fex> <t>whirred</t> <fex name="Spd">rapidly</fex> <fex name="Goal">out to sea</fex>.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Thm">The limousine</fex> <t>purred</t> <fex name="Path">forwards</fex> <fex name="Goal">into the traffic</fex>.</ex>
<ex><fex name="Thm">Loose guns</fex> <t>rumbled</t> <fex name="Area">all over the ship's deck</fex> .</ex>
<ex><fex name="Thm">The train</fex> <t>clanged</t> along <fex name="Dist">for over a thousand miles</fex>.</ex></def-root>

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Cause</fen> describes the reason for the motion. <ex>The glasses <t>clinked</t> across the table <fex name="Cause">during the tornado</fex>.</ex></def-root >
frame_elements.name: Cause

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Theme</fen> is the entity that changes location.  In sentences containing a <fen>Cause</fen>, the <fen>Theme</fen> is typically the NP Object.  In other sentences, the <fen>Theme</fen> is normally the External Argument.


<ex><fex name="Theme">Pat</fex> <t>crunched</t> over the fresh snow.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Theme

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Source</fen> is any expression which implies a definite starting-point of Motion.

<ex>The train <t>rumbled</t> <fex name="Source">out of the station</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Source

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Path</fen> is any description of a trajectory of motion which is neither a <fen>Source</fen> nor a <fen>Goal</fen>.

<ex>The truck <t>roared</t> <fex name="Path">through the tunnel</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Path

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Goal</fen> is any expression which tells where the <fen>Theme</fen> ends up as a result of the Motion.

<ex>The plates <t>clattered</t> <fex name="Goal">to the floor</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Goal

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the general <fen>Area</fen> in which motion takes place, used particularly if the motion is understood as following a complex or non-linear path.

<ex>The fly <t>buzzed</t> <fex name="Area">about the room</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Area

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Distance</fen> is any expression which characterizes the extent of Motion.  This frame element occurs very infrequently with Motion_noise verbs.

<ex>The car <t>wheezed</t> <fex name="Dist">the two miles</fex> into town.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Distance

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Speed</fen> is the rate at which the motion occurs.

<ex>My Saab <t>purrs</t> along easily <fex name="Speed">at 80 miles an hour</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Speed

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Depictive</fen> indicates the state of the <fen>Theme</fen> during Motion.

<ex>The car <t>chugged</t> across the ruts, <fex name="Dep">unstoppable</fex>.</ex>
</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Depictive

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Manner</fen> is the way in which the Motion takes place.

<ex>The drone <t>buzzed</t> <fex name="Manr">curiously</fex> across the room and vanished behind the table.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Manner

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the <fen>Means</fen> by which the <fen>Theme</fen> moves in the specified way.

<ex>The autochopper <t>whirred</t> along<fex name="Mns"> by supplementing its onboard power with solar generators</fex>.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Means

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The <fen>Result</fen> is the ultimate effect of the Motion.

<ex>The door of the empty box <t>creaked</t> <fex name="Result">open</fex> in the wind.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Result

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>This FE identifies the <fen>Degree</fen> to which the Motion occurs.

<ex>Suddenly , the pole <t>thumped</t> <fex name="Degr">really hard</fex> into an unseen object.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Degree

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Place</fen> describes the location of a more specific motion (which has <fen>Source</fen>, <fen>Path</fen>, <fen>Goal</fen>, or <fen>Area</fen>).</def-root>
frame_elements.name: Place

frame_elements.definition:
<def-root>The period of time for which the <fen>Theme</fen> moves under accompaniment of noise.

<ex>From there they <t>roared</t> northward <fex name="Duration">for about 10 minutes</fex> before turning up the beach approach onto A1.</ex></def-root>
frame_elements.name: Duration

frame_elements.definition: <def-root>The <fen>Time</fen> when the motion event takes place.  <ex>The train <t>screeched</t> into the station <fex name="Time">at half past seven</fex></ex></def-root >
frame_elements.name: Time

1046.definition: COD: move with a hissing or rushing sound.
1046.name: swish.v

6263.definition: COD: move by turning over and over on an axis.
6263.name: roll.v

Animate_being.definition: WN synset: animal, animate being, beast, brute, creature, fauna

Attribute.definition: Ontological type from which more specific attributes such as Shape and Quantity inherit.

Degree.definition: Type for expressions of degree, such as _very_, _completely_, _somewhat_ and _partially_.

Duration.definition: Marks FEs which have time-periods as fillers.

Goal.definition: Marks FEs whose fillers denote a location that is the destination of motion.

Living_thing.definition: WN synset: organism, being, living thing

Locative_relation.definition: Type for relations between events and locations.

Manner.definition: Type for expressions of the manner of an event or action: _suddenly_, _gradually_, _grudgingly_

Ontological_type.definition: Supertype for FN semantic types on FEs, corresponding roughly to nodes in other ontologies.

Relation.definition: Type for relations in general, inherited by more specific relation types.

Sentient.definition: Marks FEs whose fillers are sentient beings; dogs, definitely; bacteria, probably not; comatose people, planeria, maybe.  This is a common-sense type, with fuzzy boundaries, not a precise bio-medical category.

Source.definition: Marks FEs whose fillers depict a location as formerly occupied before motion.

State_of_affairs.definition: Type for states of affairs broadly defined, including states, events and the content of messages: _her happiness_, _your graduation_, _the Big Bang_

Time.definition: Marks FEs whose fillers denote points in time.
